extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (litigators, prosecutors) and IP counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating whether a means-plus-function claim satisfies the definiteness requirement by identifying corresponding structure in the specification (or permitted incorporated material). Focuses on when incorporation by reference can supply required structure. Useful in claim drafting, prosecution, and litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function claiming under 35 U.S.C. §112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: An element may be expressed as a means or step for performing a specified function without reciting structure, and such a claim is construed to cover the corresponding structure, material, or acts described in the specification and equivalents thereof (35 U.S.C. §112(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when a claim element invokes §112(f); doing so requires looking to the specification for corresponding structure. The doctrine allows claiming function without reciting particular structure in the claim, but displaces the requirement by importing structure from the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding structure must be disclosed in the specification; absence renders claim indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying the structure corresponding to a means-plus-function element is necessary for understanding the claim; if the specification does not disclose adequate corresponding structure, the claim is indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A generic or purely functional recital (e.g., a generic 'control' box with no indication of structure) is inadequate. If no corresponding structure can be identified in the specification, the proper result is indefiniteness (see Fiber decision affirming district court).

rubrics_metrics.name: Material incorporated by reference normally cannot supply corresponding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent a specific indication to the contrary, material incorporated by reference cannot provide the corresponding structure necessary to satisfy the definiteness requirement for a means-plus-function clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts are hesitant to find structure in incorporated material unless the specification expressly imports that structure. Attempting to rely on incorporation by reference as a substitute for disclosure in the specification is likely to fail (Fiber; consistent with Pressure Prods. Med. Supplies and Otto Bock).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted incorporation per 37 C.F.R. 1.57(d) applies only to essential material
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, 'essential material' may be incorporated by reference where it is necessary to describe the structure, material, or acts that correspond to a claimed means or step for performing a specified function as required by 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (37 C.F.R. 1.57(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the regulation allows incorporation of essential material, courts remain reluctant to treat incorporated documents as supplying corresponding structure unless incorporation is explicit and targeted. If incorporation is intended to supply structure, do so expressly and clearly in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency test: would a person skilled in the art identify the structure from the disclosure?
rubrics_metrics.description: The test for whether a structure is sufficiently disclosed is whether structure is described in the specification and, if so, whether one skilled in the art would identify the structure from that description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the PHOSITA (person having ordinary skill in the art) standard: ask whether a skilled artisan could identify the requisite structure from the specification (Default Proof Credit Card Sys. v. Home Depot example). If not, the disclosure is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must expressly point to a specific reference if relying on incorporated material for structure
rubrics_metrics.description: To rely on a structure in material incorporated by reference, the specification must expressly state in which specific reference the structure corresponding to the claimed functionality is found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice (and judicial requirement) is to make a clear, express statement in the specification naming the external reference and indicating that the structure therein is being imported to supply the corresponding structure for the means-plus-function element (see Otto Bock and Fiber guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern: merely mentioning prior art or citing references does not import their structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Simply mentioning prior art references in a patent does not suffice as a specification description to give the patentee claim to all of the structures disclosed in those references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assuming that citations or general references in the specification will permit importing detailed structure from external documents. Cases like Pressure Prods. reject claim-scope importation based on mere mention; explicit incorporation for the purpose of importing structure is required.
